transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist here. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess... they brought me in because of work. At the warehouse. I just... I keep doing things. Like, freezing with my arms up when I'm by the forklift. Or... I copy the beeping noises it makes, and the hand signals. And I move the boxes in these... patterns. Even when everyone is yelling at me to stop.
When you freeze with your arms up or copy the beeping noises, can you stop yourself from doing it, or does it feel like something you have to do?
I don't know... I just do it. It's not like I'm trying to. I just... do it.
Before you freeze your arms or copy the beeping sounds, do you feel any uncomfortable sensation, like tension or anxiety, that gets better when you do these things?
No... not really. I just... it just happens. I don't feel anything before it.
How old were you when you first started doing these things—freezing your arms, copying sounds, moving boxes in patterns? Can you remember back to when it started?
I don't really know... maybe... six months ago. All this stuff at the warehouse, the things I do... and the way I've been talking... it's just been about six months.

You said these things started about six months ago at the warehouse. But thinking back to when you were a child—before the warehouse job—did you ever have any repetitive movements, sounds, or ways of doing things that you just had to do?
No... I don't think so. I don't remember doing anything like that when I was a kid. Just... no. It's just been recently.
Besides the beeping sounds you copy from the forklift, do you ever make other sounds or noises that just come out—like throat clearing, humming, or words you don't mean to say—that you can't control?
No. Just the forklift. Nothing else.

When you copy the beeping sounds from the forklift—are those the only sounds that come out of your mouth that you don't control, or do you also find yourself making other sounds like clicking, whistling, or saying words or phrases without meaning to?
I just... I already said. It's only the forklift. I don't do any of that other stuff. Just the beeps.
You mentioned freezing your arms up by the forklift and moving boxes in patterns. Are these movements things that just happen on their own that you can't stop, like the beeping sounds?
No... I just move them that way. They don't... it doesn't just happen on its own. I just do it.

When you freeze your arms up by the forklift or move the boxes in patterns, if someone told you to stop right in that moment, could you stop immediately, or would it feel like you have to finish the movement?
I don't... I'm not really sure. Nobody's ever told me to stop. I guess I could just stop. I just... do it.
When you copy the beeping sounds from the forklift, do you feel like you have to make those sounds, or can you easily choose not to make them when you want to?
I don't know. I just... I hear it, and then I do it. I haven't really tried to stop.
When you freeze your arms up or move the boxes in patterns, does it feel like something happening to your body that you're watching, or does it feel like you're choosing to do it?
I don't... I'm not watching it happen. It's just... me doing it, I guess. I don't really think about it like that.
When you freeze your arms up by the forklift, does it feel like your arms are moving on their own without you deciding to move them, or does it feel like you are choosing to move them that way?
I don't know... I'm just doing it. They aren't moving on their own. I just... put them up there.
When you hear the forklift beeping, do you feel like you have to copy that sound right away—like an urge you can't resist—or is it more that you just naturally imitate it because it's there?
I don't really know about an urge. It's just... it's there, so I do it. I don't think about it that much.
When you move the boxes in these patterns or freeze your arms up, do you feel like it helps you feel calm or organized, or does it just feel like something your body is doing that you can't control?
I don't really know. It doesn't... make me feel anything, I guess. I'm not out of control, I just... I just do it. That's all.

When you copy the beeping sounds from the forklift, it sounds like that happens pretty automatically—you hear it and you do it. When you freeze your arms up or move the boxes in patterns, does it feel the same way—automatic and hard to stop—or does it feel different, like something you're choosing to do?

I don't really know. I guess... that's why they brought me in here. Because at the warehouse, I just keep doing it. Freezing with my arms up by the forklift... copying the hand signals and the beeping. Or moving the boxes in those little patterns. I just do it. Even when everyone is yelling at me to stop, I... I don't stop. I don't know if it's automatic. It's just what I do.
When you freeze your arms up by the forklift, does it happen suddenly and quickly like a jerk, or does it feel more slow and controlled?
I don't really know. I just... stop. I haven't really thought about if it's fast or slow. I just... freeze.
When you copy the beeping sounds from the forklift, if you tried really hard to hold it in and not make that sound, do you think you could stop yourself from making it, or would it come out anyway?
I haven't really... tried to hold it in. So I don't know. I just hear the backing up sound and... then I make it. I haven't tried to stop.
When you freeze your arms up by the forklift, does it happen suddenly like a quick twitch or jerk, or do you gradually decide to put your arms up and hold them there?
I don't think it's a twitch. I just... I don't know. I'm not really deciding to do it. My arms just... go up. I haven't really paid attention to how it happens.
